title: Six Overtimes at the Garden
dek: A waved-off buzzer-beater, five overtimes in which UConn took the lead and Syracuse answered, and a 127-117 Orange win that ended at 1:22 a.m.

tip.text: 9:36 p.m. ET (the official box score lists a 9:30 p.m. start)

setup.text: It was the fourth and last quarterfinal of a Thursday at Madison Square Garden. Third-seeded UConn, 27-3 and No. 3 in the AP poll, was playing its first game of the tournament after a double bye. Sixth-seeded Syracuse, 24-8 and No. 18, had beaten Seton Hall 89-74 the night before.

UConn had spent much of February at No. 1 in the AP poll, but it was without guard Jerome Dyson. He tore the lateral meniscus in his right knee during a 63-49 home win over Syracuse on Feb. 11 and missed the season's last 12 games. Jim Calhoun moved Kemba Walker into the starting lineup in his place.

The Huskies also had a Garden problem: they had lost their first Big East tournament game three years running. Senior Jeff Adrien later recalled that his class had never won a tournament game at the Garden.

game.text: Syracuse's Eric Devendorf had 10 points by halftime and the Orange led 18-13 early, but UConn shot 15 of 29 in the first half and took a 37-34 lead into the break.

Syracuse took over late. Arinze Onuaku's layup made it 64-57 with 3:56 left, and UConn answered with seven straight points, tying it on a Stanley Robinson follow layup with 2:25 to go. The Orange then made seven of eight free throws in the last two minutes; Kristof Ongenaet's with 27 seconds left made it 71-69, Syracuse's last lead until the sixth overtime.

The overtimes fell into a pattern: UConn took the lead in each of the first five, and Syracuse came back every time. Fouls emptied both benches. Syracuse lost Ongenaet, Onuaku and Rick Jackson by early in the fourth overtime and put 6-foot-7 freshman Kris Joseph, who had not played in regulation, at center, a position he had not played in college. Walk-on Justin Thomas replaced Devendorf when he fouled out in the fifth. UConn lost Robinson in the third overtime, Hasheem Thabeet in the fourth, Gavin Edwards in the fifth and A.J. Price in the sixth.

As Thursday turned into Friday, the Garden's game-operations crew played 'After Midnight,' 'All Night Long' and 'In the Midnight Hour,' and the scoreboard simply read period eight. Most of the sellout crowd of 19,375 was still there for the sixth overtime.

sequence.text: Craig Austrie's jumper misses. Kemba Walker, one of the smallest players on the floor, grabs the loose ball and lays it in. Tie game, 1.1 seconds left.

After a Syracuse timeout, Paul Harris runs the baseline and throws long. Gavin Edwards gets a hand on it and deflects it right to Eric Devendorf, who fires from about 28 feet as the backboard's red end-of-game lights come on. It drops. Devendorf leaps onto a courtside table and Syracuse celebrates, but officials John Cahill and Bob Donato study replay after replay for about five minutes and rule the ball was still on his fingertips at 0.0. Overtime.

UConn led 80-76 late in the first overtime. Andy Rautins hits a 3, Stanley Robinson makes a free throw, and Jonny Flynn goes the length of the floor and dishes to Rick Jackson for a tying dunk. Walker's 3 at the horn is short.
Tied at 87 at the end of the second overtime, Walker lets fly from just inside midcourt. It hits the back of the rim and bounces away.
UConn scored the first six points of the third overtime and still leads 98-95 after A.J. Price makes one of two free throws.

Rautins comes around a Jackson screen, takes Flynn's pass on the wing and buries an off-balance 3. Price misses a 3 at the other end and Jeff Adrien can't convert the rebound: a fourth overtime, making it the longest game in Big East tournament history.
Price misses a drive in the final seconds. Paul Harris gets two chances at the rim at the other end and can't finish either. Still tied.
With Robinson and Thabeet already fouled out, UConn goes ahead on a jumper by reserve Scottie Haralson, his first field goal of the night.
Flynn splits a ball screen, draws a foul from Haralson and makes both free throws.
Price's long 3 bounces off the rim to Adrien, whose jumper at the horn is short. A sixth overtime.
Syracuse wins the tip and runs a set play: Rautins comes off a screen and hits a 3 about 10 seconds in. It is the Orange's first lead since regulation.
Paul Harris scores 10 of Syracuse's 17 points in the period, and once Syracuse goes up 118-110, UConn gets no closer than six. The horn sounds at 1:22 a.m. Friday: Syracuse 127, UConn 117.

numbers.label: overtimes, tied for the second-longest game in Division I history, one short of Cincinnati-Bradley's seven in 1981
final horn, 3 hours and 46 minutes after the 9:36 p.m. tip
combined points, a Big East tournament record; 102 came in the overtimes
minutes played by Syracuse's Jonny Flynn, a school record, out of a possible 70
players fouled out, four on each team

quotes.text: We lost the game because we turned the ball over 27 times and couldn't make a foul shot.
It would have been a lot better if they just counted Eric's shot and we could have gone home 2 hours ago.
I could just see that the ball was still touching the fingertips of Devendorf as the 0.00 showed up on the clock.
I was real relieved when they waved it off. ... I thought I was going to be a dead man on campus.
quotes.role: UConn forward who deflected the inbound pass

aftermath.text: Syracuse played again that Friday night and beat West Virginia 74-69 in overtime, then lost the final to Louisville 76-66 on Saturday. Flynn won the Gavitt Trophy as the tournament's most outstanding player.

UConn went into the NCAA tournament as a No. 1 seed. Its 103-47 rout of Chattanooga in Philadelphia was its first postseason win in three years; the six-overtime loss had been its fifth straight postseason defeat.
The Huskies won four NCAA games to reach the Final Four in Detroit, where Michigan State beat them 82-73 on April 4.

legacy.text: It was the longest game in Big East history and, at six overtimes, tied for the second-longest in NCAA history, behind Cincinnati's seven-overtime win over Bradley in 1981, played before the shot clock.

Two years later Kemba Walker, whose putback forced the first overtime, scored 130 points in the 2011 Big East tournament, breaking the single-tournament record of 84 that Syracuse's Eric Devendorf had set in 2009.
When UConn and Syracuse went to overtime again in the 2011 semifinal, Walker said he thought about six right away. Many fans at the Garden that night wore T-shirts commemorating the 127-117 marathon.
Jim Boeheim later called it the best game he had ever been part of.

unsure: No official play-by-play for this game was found: UConn's official 2008-09 file (uconn_ftp .../2008-2009/game31.html) and Syracuse's box page carry box scores only. Where the site's ESPN play-by-play clock disagrees with the AP story, Syracuse athletics and the Daily Orange, the sequence uses the published contemporaneous times (see conflicts).
AP says Devendorf jumped onto the 'courtside press table'; the Daily Orange and the Fox oral history say the scorer's table. Draft says 'a courtside table.'

Distance of Rautins' tying 3 in the third overtime: the Daily Orange says both 'about 22 feet out on the wing' and 'well beyond the NBA arc'; Leo Rautins later called it 'like a 25-footer.' No distance used.

AP says Paul Harris 'had two shots blocked' at the end of the fourth overtime; the site play-by-play logs one block (Gavin Edwards) and the Fox oral history says Harris had two chances at the rim and couldn't finish. Draft uses the latter.
Previous Big East tournament combined-points record: 189 per Syracuse's 2009 recap (Villanova 96, Pittsburgh 93 in 1998) vs. 194 per the 2014 Fox oral history. Not used.
Devendorf recalled (Fox, 2014) fouling out in the fourth overtime; the site play-by-play and Syracuse's recap put his fifth foul in the fifth. Draft follows the play-by-play.
Claims about Onuaku's free-throw percentage that season (Fox: 30 percent; orangehoops.org: 16 percent in Big East play) were not verified and are not used.
No Wikimedia Commons photo of this game was found, and archive.org's Daily Campus scans end in 1987, so photos and newspaper are empty.

Two more full-game uploads exist (vrqFggZjDZA, NewJoel, 3:03:22; p9RgGPrCDyw, iDoItBIGson, 3:05:01) and a clip billed as Bill Raftery's reaction to the waved-off shot (Gzs_OWgAZi8). Not viewed and not added.
